tweets.text:
time is an underrated part of risk management when trading lower timeframes

when i enter a trade expecting a sharp move, i want price to react relatively quickly

if Bitcoin is sitting around my entry for too long without moving in the direction i expected, i start questioning the setup

the advantage of trading lower timeframes is that you can recognize when something isn't working much earlier

sometimes i'll exit a trade simply because it's taking too long to play out, even if my stop hasn't been hit

price and time both matter when deciding whether a trade is still worth taking

tweets.text:
It's not obscene. It's not about him, and his circumstances in isolation. It's about millions of people recognising themselves in his reaction - that they can work hard, do everything 'right' and feel let down by a system that constantly demands more and gives less.
Then to be mocked, and looked down upon by the sociopaths of our age, told their lives are not serious, told to work harder, they just don't want it enough. That your own life, circumstance and dignity can be used as the butt of a joke by someone so disconnected from reality that they don't see you as a person, but as content

The dehumanising of the average person, and experience, by the systems we were told would reward us for our hard work. It's not that people feel entitled to millions, it's that they feel robbed of the dignity of their own humanity and moments like this are a reflection of the machine shoving it back in their face. That someone thinks it is funny, or okay, to disrupt a man doing his job, to joke about robbing him - to turn that into content, to monetise it and make his reaction the joke. The streamer is a reflection of that dehumanising machine spitting back in their face in the form of another person. It's everything wrong with our current culture, where it's not only enough to have people struggling to get by, but the system now encourages itself to mock, demean and put down that daily struggle that many people live with.

And no, this isn't an isolated issue, it's a cultural shift. The president of the United States recently joked on camera about how people couldn't afford to visit him at Mar a Lago. The system mocks from all angles and for the average person daily survival can feel like a humiliation ritual, having to put aside your dignity in the name of providing for those that you love. And millions of people will wake up every day, and gladly make that choice. Swallow their pride and do what needs to be done. All they ask is that they are not mocked for the decision to do so.

So no, it's not an over-reaction, it's a very concentrated reflection of how people are feeling.
